context:
Goal: no live agent loses its worktree mid-task.
Problem (risk): at merge, merge/merge.py:1984-1992 (cut_local, then remove_held_tree) frees a worktree's own agent lock once the worktree is merged and idle for 30 minutes (janitor/sweep.py:474-498 and 793-795). A quiet reviewer writes no git, so it reads as idle.
Based on (code): janitor/sweep.py own_agent_lock_verdict.
Based on (ruling): decision when-a-worktree-may-be-removed, line 7: no lock holds a worktree that a merge removes. Asked again because the lost-worktree incident of 2026-11-06 is the harm that line allows.
Departs from: main, where a merge frees an agent's own lock after 30 idle minutes. Option a keeps the lock while its agent is alive.

options.gain: A live reviewer's worktree is safe.
options.label: A merge never frees a lock whose agent is alive; the record changes to say so (recommended)
options.lose: Merged worktrees with a live agent stay until that session ends.

options.label: Keep the code, and rewrite the record to match it
options.lose: A quiet live reviewer can still lose its worktree.

short: Merge frees a live agent's worktree lock?
title: Should a merge ever free a worktree lock whose agent is still alive?
why: A quiet reviewer writes no git for 30 minutes, so the merge reads its worktree as idle and can remove it mid-task.
